title: Clean a messy contact list into JSON
summary: Tidy names, emails and Nigerian phone numbers from a pasted table, drop invalid rows and duplicates, and report what was dropped.
instructions:
Below is a pasted contact table, one row per line, with the fields id | name | email | phone. Clean it and return a JSON object with the fields contacts, duplicates_removed and invalid_rows.

Cleaning rules:
- name: remove spaces at the start and end and turn every run of spaces inside it into one space. Keep the letters as written.
- email: write it in lower case. It is valid only if it has exactly one @ with at least one character before it and at least one after it, and no spaces.
- phone: first remove all spaces and hyphens. It is valid only if what is left is either a local number (a 0 followed by 10 digits) or an international number (+234 followed by 10 digits). Write every valid phone in the international form: +234 and the 10 digits, without the leading 0.
- A row with an invalid email or an invalid phone is invalid. Leave it out of contacts and list its id in invalid_rows, as a number, in the order of the table.
- Among the valid rows, a row whose cleaned email equals the email of an earlier valid row is a duplicate. Keep the first one and leave the later one out of contacts. duplicates_removed is the number of rows left out as duplicates.
- contacts has one object per kept row, in the order of the table, with the fields name, email and phone.

Reply with the JSON object only: no code fences, no explanation before or after it.

How it is checked: your JSON must fit the published schema. Then each important value in it is compared with a hidden answer key. The score is the share of values that match, and the reward is paid only for a score of 100.
